summary.headline: Shriram Finance Q4 FY26 PAT rose 40.86% YoY to INR3,013.57 crores; management guides 18% AUM growth for FY27 but will revisit after Q1.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered strong profitability, with PAT up 40.86% YoY to INR3,013.57 crores and NIM up to 8.61%, while AUM grew 14.85% YoY to INR3,02,273.75 crores. Gross Stage 3 edged up to 4.58% from 4.55% a year ago, and Stage 2 plus Stage 3 rose sequentially in CV, PV and MSME. MUFG Bank completed a preferential allotment on April 8, 2026, taking a 20% fully diluted stake, and the board recommended a final dividend of INR6 per share. Management budgets 18% AUM growth and 8.5% NIM for FY27, but said Q1 FY27 is hard to predict and it will revisit guidance after Q1, with credit cost unchanged for now.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles (CV)
segments.commentary: Management said new CV financing improved with sales, and used CV is the largest franchise; FY27 CV growth is guided at 15% to 18%. Stage 2 plus Stage 3 in CV rose about 17 bps QoQ per an analyst.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles (PV)
segments.commentary: Management expects PV growth above 20% in FY27, against a Q4 slowdown in used PV financing that management attributed to focus on CV. Gross Stage 2 plus Stage 3 also rose in PV.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Growth moderated to about 10% to 12% in FY26 from 25% to 30% earlier; FY27 guidance is 13% to 15% with a cautious stance. Management said most large MSME tickets are mortgage-backed.

segments.name: Tractors and farm equipment
segments.commentary: Expected to see demand decline in FY27 on a weaker monsoon forecast (94% of LPA per IMD), though used tractor financing is expected to hold up. Tractor sales rose 22.87% YoY in Q4 industry data cited on the call.

segments.name: New vehicle financing
segments.commentary: New vehicles are about 15% of disbursements, and management expects this to rise by another 5 to 10 percentage points over the next two quarters; it is not expected to reach 30% to 35%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth budgeted at 18%, with management reaffirming it on the call; management said Q1 FY27 may be lower and guidance will be revisited after Q1 results.
Cost-to-income ratio guided to 26% to 27% over the long term; opex to stay around this level, with headcount to rise from about 76,000 toward 80,000 over the next couple of quarters.
Budgeted NIM of 8.5% for FY27 despite expected cost-of-funds benefit; management said NIM will expand, with some benefit passed on to customers.
Credit cost: no change in estimate for now; management will revisit after Q1 FY27, with any stress expected to show after November-December 2026 if fuel prices and monsoon disappoint.
Borrowing: company is not in a hurry to tap the bond market at AAA; it may borrow only after four to five months, and expects lower cost of borrowing in the coming year.
capex_capacity: MUFG Bank preferential allotment of 47,11,21,055 shares at INR840.93 per share, totalling INR396.18 billion, completed April 8, 2026, giving MUFG 20% on a fully diluted basis.
Capital adequacy ratio at 20.4% currently, rising to about 34% post the equity infusion.
Liquidity of about INR13,000 crores at quarter end; an equity inflow of about INR40,000 crores was expected in the first week of April, which management said explained the lower liquidity.
Headcount fell to about 76,000 from about 79,000 a year earlier; management plans to increase it toward 80,000.
demand_pricing: Industry sales growth in Q4 FY26 cited on the call: CV +18.86%, PV +13.22%, two-wheelers +26.39%, tractors +22.87%, construction equipment -16.02%.
Management said April 2026 was normal with no challenges seen; supply-side raw material delays were noted but no slowdown in customer transport activity.
Cost of funds: last bond issued in December quarter at about 7.5%; management estimated March-quarter issuance would have cost about 25 bps more at the earlier AA+ rating.
Management expects lower borrowing costs in the coming year, with deposit rates cut and better risk weight for bank borrowings after the upgrade.
Management said pass-through of any cost-of-funds benefit to borrowers will be used to retain customers and grow, without a fixed split.

qa_highlights.question: Is AUM growth of 18% for FY27 on AUM or disbursements, and what is the opex and credit cost guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: 18% refers to AUM growth; opex to stay around 26% to 27% cost-to-income; credit cost seen as manageable for now, to be revisited after Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 GS2 plus GS3 rise sequentially in CV, PV and MSME, and will credit cost rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retail cash-flow fluctuations are normal and provisions are priced in; coverage was increased slightly; stress, if any, expected after November-December depending on fuel prices and monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the budgeted NIM and how much of the cost-of-funds benefit goes to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM budgeted at 8.5%; management aims to protect NIM and pass on benefit only if needed for growth; NIM will expand in practice, though the budget is conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Why did used PV financing slow in Q4, and what is the PV growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the slowdown to focus on CV and expects PV growth above 20% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What share of disbursements is new vehicle financing and how will it scale?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% of disbursements now; expected to rise by 5 to 10 percentage points over the next two quarters, not to 30% to 35%.

qa_highlights.question: Will MUFG increase its stake before the 24-month lock-in ends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment, saying nothing has been discussed and it is too early, less than one month after allotment.

risks_watch: Fuel price increases tied to West Asia conflict and a monsoon forecast of 94% of LPA could hit transporter cash flows, with stress expected after November-December 2026.
Stage 2 plus Stage 3 rose sequentially in CV, PV and MSME; gross Stage 3 up to 4.58% from 4.54% in Q3 FY26.
Q1 FY27 is expected to be the hardest quarter to predict; growth guidance to be revisited after Q1 results.
MUFG's 20% stake and its 24-month restriction on secondary-market purchases; management declined to discuss any future increase.
Margin expansion depends on cost-of-funds benefit versus pass-through to customers; the NIM budget is 8.5% against Q4 actual of 8.61%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Q4 results and the capital position, but cautious on the outlook. Management repeatedly declined to quantify FY27 credit cost, fuel-price or stake-change scenarios, deferring to Q1 results.
key_quotes: We will be growing at 18%. Yes. We will be growing at 18%.
But definitely, after the first quarter, first three months, we will relook at our budget.
First quarter of this financial year is going to be most difficult to predict, but we are quite hopeful to come out with good numbers.

growth.why: Management budgets 18% AUM growth for FY27 (reaffirmed, but to be revisited after Q1) and 8.5% NIM, backed by disbursement momentum (Q4 disbursements +14.91% YoY) and CV/PV/MSME segment guidance, with no hard capacity additions or order-book style backing disclosed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 NIM was 8.61% vs FY27 budget of 8.5%, and management said NIM will expand in practice as cost of funds falls (last bond ~7.5%, cost of liabilities 8.59% from 8.69% in Q3), though some benefit goes to customers.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management budgets 18% AUM growth for FY27 (AUM +14.85% YoY to INR3,02,273.75 crores) with CV guided at 15-18%, PV above 20% and MSME 13-15%, though Q1 FY27 may be lower and guidance is to be revisited after Q1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex or new plant discussed; the company is asset-light and the capital raise (MUFG INR396.18 billion, CAR 20.4% rising to about 34%) is equity for balance sheet, not physical capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reaffirmed 18% AUM growth and 8.5% NIM budget, described as conservative, but said it will only revisit guidance after Q1 FY27 with Q1 possibly lower and no upgrade signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Stage 3 at 4.58% gross (up from 4.54% in Q3), Stage 2 plus Stage 3 rising sequentially in CV, PV and MSME, and stress could appear after Nov-Dec 2026 if fuel prices and the 94% of LPA monsoon forecast disappoint.

rows.label: New vehicle financing mix rising
rows.why: New vehicles are about 15% of disbursements and management expects a rise of another 5 to 10 percentage points, not to 30% to 35%.

rows.label: Post-MUFG equity leverage drop
rows.why: Leverage at 3.82 times is expected to fall to about 2.4 times and CAR to about 34% after the equity infusion of INR396.18 billion from MUFG (20% fully diluted).

rows.label: Lower borrowing cost in FY27
rows.why: Last bond at about 7.5% in the December quarter, a better risk weight after the upgrade and deposit rate cuts are expected, although the company will wait four to five months before borrowing.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q4 profit (PAT +40.86% YoY to INR3,013.57 crores), capital and funding, but cautious on FY27 credit cost and Q1 visibility; analysts pressed on credit cost, Stage 2 plus Stage 3 rising in CV, PV and MSME, and PV slowdown.
